\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعذر} (taʿadhdhara)}{تعذر (taʿadhdhara)}]{\ar{تعذر} (taʿadhdhara) — to prove impossible}

\label{lesson:AR-C407-taadhdhara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to lack, then the Arabic for a procedure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعذر}}
\textbf{\ar{تعذر}} — \emph{taʿadhdhara} — \textquotedblleft{}to prove impossible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعذر} \ar{علينا} \ar{السفر} \ar{بسبب} \ar{الطقس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿadhdhara ʿalaynā as-safar bi-sabab aṭ-ṭaqs.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Travelling proved impossible for us because of the weather.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتعذر}, \emph{yataʿadhdhar}.

It takes \ar{على} for the person: \ar{تعذر} \ar{عليه} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعذر}} (\emph{taʿadhdhara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-dh-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to excuse\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V; Lane gives it for an affair that became hard to bring about, and so impracticable: to prove impossible.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿadhdhara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿadhdhara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿadhdhara ʿalaynā as-safar bi-sabab aṭ-ṭaqs.} — Travelling proved impossible for us because of the weather.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to lack, then the Arabic for a procedure, then say \emph{taʿadhdhara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تعذر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To prove impossible\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استلزم} (istalzama)}{استلزم (istalzama)}]{\ar{استلزم} (istalzama) — to entail}

\label{lesson:AR-C407-istalzama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a procedure, then the Arabic for to prove impossible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استلزم}}
\textbf{\ar{استلزم}} — \emph{istalzama} — \textquotedblleft{}to entail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يستلزم} \ar{المشروع} \ar{وقتا} \ar{طويلا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yastalzimu al-mashrūʿ waqtan ṭawīlan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The project entails a long time.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستلزم}, \emph{yastalzim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استلزم}} (\emph{istalzama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-z-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to cling, to stick to\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to call for what must cling to a thing: to entail.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a procedure, then the Arabic for to prove impossible, then say \emph{istalzama} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تجنب} (tajannaba)}{تجنب (tajannaba)}]{\ar{تجنب} (tajannaba) — to avoid}

\label{lesson:AR-C407-tajannaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to prove impossible, then the Arabic for to entail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تجنب}}
\textbf{\ar{تجنب}} — \emph{tajannaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to avoid\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تجنب} \ar{الرجل} \ar{الطريق} \ar{المزدحم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tajannaba ar-rajul aṭ-ṭarīq al-muzdaḥim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man avoided the crowded road.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتجنب}, \emph{yatajannab}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تجنب}} (\emph{tajannaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-n-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to put aside, to turn away\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to put oneself to one side of a thing: to avoid it. \ar{بجانب}, beside, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to prove impossible, then the Arabic for to entail, then say \emph{tajannaba} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تفادى} (tafādā)}{تفادى (tafādā)}]{\ar{تفادى} (tafādā) — to avert}

\label{lesson:AR-C407-tafada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to entail, then the Arabic for to avoid.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تفادى}}
\textbf{\ar{تفادى}} — \emph{tafādā} — \textquotedblleft{}to avert\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تفادى} \ar{الطفل} \ar{الكرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tafādā aṭ-ṭifl al-kura.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child got out of the way of the ball.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتفادى}, \emph{yatafādā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تفادى}} (\emph{tafādā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-d-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to ransom\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI. How its sense, keeping clear of a thing, grew from ransoming is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to entail, then the Arabic for to avoid, then say \emph{tafādā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طرأ} (ṭaraʾa)}{طرأ (ṭaraʾa)}]{\ar{طرأ} (ṭaraʾa) — to arise unexpectedly}

\label{lesson:AR-C407-taraa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to avoid, then the Arabic for to avert.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طرأ}}
\textbf{\ar{طرأ}} — \emph{ṭaraʾa} — \textquotedblleft{}to arise unexpectedly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طرأ} \ar{تغيير} \ar{على} \ar{الخطة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭaraʾa taghyīr ʿalā al-khiṭṭa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A change came up in the plan.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يطرأ}, \emph{yaṭraʾ}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{طرأ} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طرأ}} (\emph{ṭaraʾa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-r-ʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}to come upon unexpectedly\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ṭaraʾa} is a Form I verb: to come from far off without warning, to arise.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to avoid, then the Arabic for to avert, then say \emph{ṭaraʾa} again
\end{itemize}
